remove.point: Stop fetching PT Sans 400 italic for one emphasised title inside bold headings. On /fi/portfolio/ the only PT Sans italic text is the 34-character em 'Beginning Ruby on Rails E-Commerce' in a 700-weight heading. The browser downloads the 400 italic file (about 42 KiB) and then fakes the bold. Setting headings' em to font-style: normal, or using quotes, removes a whole face from that page with no loss of meaning. See O-c1.

two_x.point: Unchanged from critique 5c2e92ac and already recorded under O-c1/O-c2: make the first paint the final type. Preload the first-viewport faces and add metric-matched Georgia/Arial fallbacks. Now that unicode-range is fixed, the evidence is sharper: render delay rises about 150 to 300 ms per extra face before first paint (/fi/ with 3 faces 1804 ms LCP; /about/ with 5 faces 2256 ms). Strongest counter-argument: preload competes with the render-blocking CSS on slow links and may cost first paint; measure it against the 2000 ms budget before keeping it.

short_of_references.reference: docs/design/references.md, First 10 s: CSS Wizardry (system faces, 'fast by design')
short_of_references.point: Unchanged gap, recorded as O-c2: CSS Wizardry's first screen needs no web-font request. Ours now needs 3 to 6 latin faces (123 to 194 KiB), down from 6 to 10, and content pages still miss the 2000 ms LCP budget by up to 405 ms.
Stripe Dot Dev reaches LCP 0.9 s and CLS 0.001 with self-hosted woff2. Ours reaches 1.8 to 2.4 s and CLS up to 0.137 on /portfolio/, where the shift cause is 'Web font loaded'.
